one_liner: Navy civilian analyst at the Washington Navy Yard tracking cost, schedule and performance of submarine construction, maintenance or modernization programs and briefing senior leaders.
fit_summary: The specialized experience is narrow: a year of GS-11-level program analysis for submarine construction, maintenance or modernization, plus SCI eligibility. Daniel's resume shows no naval or defense acquisition program work and no clearance, so he likely would not be rated qualified.
eligibility: Open to the public, so no federal status is needed. However, this is a public notice flyer, not a live vacancy: you must follow its separate 'How to Apply' directions, and positions may never be filled.

You need one year of specialized experience at the NH-02/GS-11 level conducting program analysis on submarine construction, maintenance or modernization programs. This can be federal, private-sector or public-sector experience.
The position requires Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access, which means a Top Secret-level investigation and U.S. citizenship.
Resumes are limited to two pages, and all qualifications must be met before you are considered.
strategy: First, ask yourself honestly whether any IEM work touched Navy, shipyard, submarine or defense acquisition programs. If none did, treat this as a low-odds application and prioritize program analyst postings at FEMA, DHS, or Virginia VDEM that value emergency-management analysis.
If you do apply, read the flyer's 'How to Apply' section closely, since applications are not accepted through the flyer itself. Submit between Oct 27 and Nov 16, 2026.

Frame your IEM work in program-analysis terms: analyzing program cost, schedule and performance; evaluating effectiveness and compliance; and producing reports and briefings for government clients. List hours per week and dates for each job.
Use the posting's key terms, such as 'program analysis' and 'evaluation methodology', where they truly describe his work, and keep the resume to two tight pages.
His resume lists no clearance; if he has ever held one, state the level and status at the top.
Set up USAJOBS saved searches for 'Program Analyst' and 'Emergency Management Specialist' at GS-9/11 in the DC region. That way you can apply where your background fits directly.
resume_bullets: Tracked spending and order status in Excel pivot-table reports (2021–2022).
Delivered detailed notes used to write after-action reports for FEMA full-scale exercises.
interview_questions: Describe a time you analyzed a program's cost, schedule or performance problem and recommended a resolution.
How would you get up to speed on submarine maintenance or modernization programs and the DoD acquisition process?
Tell us about briefing senior leaders on findings they didn't want to hear.
How do you build working relationships with contractors and other stakeholders to keep a project on track?
watch_outs: The specialized experience is submarine-specific, and without it you will likely be found not qualified.
SCI clearance is required, and investigations can take many months.
This is an anticipatory flyer: there may be no actual hires, and no Notice of Result letters are sent.
Overstating experience can make you ineligible, so frame your work accurately.
